newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX natgas still mostly up late on technicals.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX natgas still mostly up late on technicals.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures remained mostly higher late Tuesday morning in moderate trade, with technical buying and short covering still buoying the front of the complex despite reports of softer cash.
At 1430 EST, January was still up by 15.3 cents at $3.375 per million British thermal units, while February was 9.8 cents higher at $3.11. Others were mixed, with some 1998s off.

"I think we're going to trade in this $3.10-3.50 range (basis January) for a while, but if we get any (cold) weather ahead of expiration, you'll see people buying it again," said one Houston-based trader.

While few expected cash to move far near-term, with forecasts for above-normal Midwest and Eastern temperatures into next week, traders said low stocks and an uncertain winter ahead should be enough to temper the bears.
Technical traders still saw support in January at $3.11 and then at $3.04, with trendline buying likely in the $2.70s. Resistance was seen in the remaining gap between $3.44 and $3.46.
In the cash, Gulf Coast prices slipped Tuesday by 10 cents to about the $3.20 level. Midcon pipes were down five to 10 cents to the $3.15-20 area.
NYMEX said 26,328 Hub contracts traded by 1405 EST. Hub open interest on Dec 9 fell 3,720 contracts to 143,938.
NYMEX Alberta natgas remained untraded at 1405 EST.
Alberta open interest on Dec 9 fell one lot to 247.
NYMEX Permian natgas also was untraded at 1405 EST.
Permian open interest on Dec 9 was unchanged at 89.
On the KCBT, January firmed 10.5 cents to $3.20, while February was nine cents higher at $2.94. The East/West spread widened by 4.8 cents to 17.5 cents (NYMEX premium).
